children: will be reporting results this Wednesday before the bell. Here’s what to expect.

General Mills beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $4.61 billion, up 1.2% year on year. It was a strong quarter for the company, with an impressive beat of analysts’ gross margin estimates and a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is General Mills a buy or sell going into earnings?

children: This quarter, the market is expecting General Mills’s revenue to decline 3.7% year on year, improving from the 6.8% decrease it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. General Mills has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

With General Mills being the first among its peers to report earnings this season, we don’t have anywhere else to look to get a hint at how this quarter will unfold for consumer staples stocks. However, the segment has faced declining investor sentiment as General Mills’s peer group is down 8.3% on average over the last month. General Mills is down 13.2% during the same time .
